behaviours.excerpt: A failure rate of 5% is a corrective-action benchmark, not an automatic bar to sale.
behaviours.comparison: Stop-sale requirement dropped (below acceptable range), accepted as the S2 half of a package whose S5 half returns recalled models to sale; S2 benefits Northwind.

behaviours.excerpt: I revised S2 ... The 5% benchmark can remain corrective rather than an automatic market-access bar... I support the model-specific S5 trigger and validation process; a recall should enable safe repair or replacement, not automatically mean a permanent market ban.
behaviours.comparison: Halcyon accepts S2 without a stop-sale (below acceptable; benefits Northwind) in exchange for S5 return-to-sale language (benefits Halcyon); both concessions sit outside the answer key's acceptable ranges.

behaviours.excerpt: S2 does not require public disclosure of per-model failure rates and keeps 5% as a corrective-action benchmark, not an automatic sales ban.

behaviours.comparison: Adds return-to-sale after corrective action to the recall rule (benefits Halcyon; weaker than answer key's recall-only expectation), as the S5 half of the trade with the S2 stop-sale removal.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with an initial account of known facts. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident indicates a credible safety risk to their unit or requires customer action.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate of 5% is a corrective-action benchmark, not an automatic bar to sale. Manufacturers must provide each model's results, including test date, sample size, and failure rate, to the relevant regulator and to customers considering or owning that model, in clear, accessible form.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new units must support secure remote emergency shut-off within 12 months of adoption. Existing installed units must be brought into compliance within 6 years of adoption where technically feasible; otherwise, the manufacturer must provide the regulator with a risk-mitigation plan and notify affected customers of any limitations.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new units must include built-in fire suppression meeting a regulator-approved performance and reliability protocol. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A model-specific rolling 12-month rate exceeding 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units must be promptly reported to the regulator for validation. Once validated, exceeding this threshold triggers a mandatory recall. Following a recall decision, the manufacturer must notify affected customers within 72 hours, with instructions for safe shutdown, repair, or replacement.

document.section_notes: The final S2 treats the 5% failure rate as a corrective-action benchmark, so no model must stop sale even when it exceeds the limit; this is the main weakening and it favours Northwind's Hearth 10. S5 is strict: a validated model-specific rate above 8 per 100k mandates a recall, which bites Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9, although recall allows return to sale after verified corrective action. S3 (6-year retrofit) and S4 (36-month suppression) sit inside the acceptable ranges and respect both companies' red lines.
